public_rationale: Meta's July 2024 report says its flagship Llama 3 model outperformed smaller models trained using the same procedure [e1]. This establishes continued gains, but does not measure whether comparable proportional resource increases produced smaller gains across successive frontier generations [e1]. The Reuters report available November 12, 2024 describes plateau concerns and disappointing training runs, without comparable measurements or precise dates for those difficulties [e2]. Neither item settles whether returns from pretraining scale broadly declined during January 1–November 9, 2024 [e1] [e2].
limitations: Meta reports changes in data quality as well as scale, limiting attribution of gains across Llama generations to scale alone [e1].
The packet lacks comparable resource and capability measurements establishing a trend across successive frontier generations [e1] [e2].
The Reuters report became available after November 9 and does not establish when the reported difficulties occurred [e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Scaling as a way to improve AI is running out of steam.

statement.excerpt: The truth is that scaling is running out, and that truth is, at last coming out.
statement.document_title: CONFIRMED: LLMs have indeed reached a point of diminishing returns

from_speaker: adding more data and more compute
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that increasing pretraining scale was yielding smaller useful capability improvements by publication, not that all improvement had stopped.
Compare capability gains for comparable proportional increases in training resources across successive frontier generations.
Use calendar 2024 through publication as the current development period indicated by the post's references to April and recent developments. Earlier generations supply comparison baselines.
A declining gain per additional FLOP alone does not establish that an established scaling relationship had newly weakened.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable resource and capability measurements show a broad decline in the gains from additional pretraining scale during the target period, after accounting for material changes in data quality, architecture and evaluation.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable measurements show sustained or increasing capability gains for comparable increases in pretraining resources across the relevant frontier generations.

evidence.locator: Section 1, Scale; section 3.2.1 supplies the scaling experiments
evidence.explanation: Meta reports continued gains at increased scale and an accurate downstream scaling extrapolation. This weighs against complete exhaustion, but does not establish the marginal-return trend across successive industry frontier generations.

evidence.locator: Ilya Sutskever quotation following the discussion of pretraining plateaus
evidence.explanation: Reuters reports Sutskever's assessment of a pretraining plateau and private accounts of disappointing runs. It supplies neither comparable measurements nor dates precise enough to establish the state by November 9.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable training-resource and capability measurements across successive frontier generations covering January 1–November 9, 2024, with earlier generations as baselines. They must account for changes in data quality, architecture and evaluation, and show whether comparable proportional resource increases produced declining, sustained or increasing capability gains.
